outline.h2: Sign #3: Are Your Floors Actually Sloping?
outline.notes: Question-form. Marble test (roll a marble across the floor). Level app on a 4-foot straightedge. Anything over 1 inch of slope across 10 feet = foundation issue. Add note on Victorian homes where some slope is original settling, not active.

outline.h2: Sign #4: What Do Gaps Between Walls and Trim Mean?
outline.notes: Question-form. Gap opening at baseboards, crown molding, or between walls and ceilings indicates active differential settlement. Especially at corners of the house. Common failure pattern in Bernal Heights hillside homes and post-1906 Marina construction.

outline.h2: Sign #5: Is Water Pooling Near Your Foundation?
outline.notes: Question-form. Grading issues, failed drainage, uphill neighbors, and old clay drain tile all send water toward foundations. Moisture in crawl spaces + efflorescence (white mineral deposits) on concrete = active water intrusion. Long-term water = foundation deterioration.
